narrative: The author consolidates a leveraged portfolio into higher-conviction holdings while questioning near-term AI spending economics. Healthcare and commercial biotechnology become the preferred contrast to struggling technology themes. KURA additions are disclosed, and DERM receives the most complete fresh fundamental pitch. The DERM discussion subsequently acknowledges a previously overlooked legacy patent cliff, but the author maintains that Emrosi can drive the thesis independently. WGS is explicitly trimmed to fund other opportunities rather than described as a new entry. BDSX receives a late-window valuation and product-quality endorsement. Macro commentary remains conditionally constructive on equities while skeptical that cooler yields alone will repair AI demand concerns.

$DERM https://t.co/BGB7xPDiv3

Saturday pitch time $DERM

DERM is a small cap operating with 1) a legacy portfolio of commercial dermatology products, but more importantly 2) a growing Rosacea treatment franchise in Emrosi that is the primary growth driver of the company moving forward

Their recent results showed:
1) a reacceleration in Emrosi script volumes
2) cost discipline as costs were flat YoY vs strong revenue growth leading to positive EBITDA
3) expansion in coverage and rising ASPs leading to strong trends for more patients to get the drug + drive higher revenues
4) also in recent earnings they discussed they are open to partnering on non-US territories and could license the drug out to a partner to commercialize. That's additional high margin revenue that is not currently accounted for in my conservative peak sales estimate

I think the biggest bear case is that the drug isn't necessarily something novel.
And so the bear thesis is a new entrant can come in and try to replicate, but:
1) they have patents that would hopefully hold up
2) they have a head start to market, and given they already have a portfolio of legacy derm products, they already have a salesforce and know the physician network
3) have extremely superior results to the standard of care Oracea in a ph3 trial

Oracea did $300M sales for ~30% of TAM in 2023
Emrosi is a superior drug and even with a conservative $200M peak sales figure, the stock is currently trading at 1X Emrosi peak sales, and that doesn't even include $40M current revenues from their legacy portfolio of derm drugs.
Also, that Oracea $300M figure is just for US. No intl revenues. Which Emrosi is considering/pursuing.

The stock's valuation is cheap. Yes, competition can come. But for now they're in a solid position.

Also, the stock technically looks good as it climbs out of a base and chews through a key resistance level. We had a big volume 3 week rally, followed by a 3 week low volume pullback to tap the 50SMA and hold the 9EMA into close.

Base case (conservative): Emrosi $200M peak sales (US), legacy revenues $20M, 2X peak sales = $15 PT (2X)
Bull case: Emrosi $400M peak sales (US + Intl), legacy revenues $40M, 2X peak sales = $30 PT (4X)

$DERM

Didn't realize DERM legacy revenues so close to patent cliff
Either way, the thesis doesn't depend on legacy revenues
They're only $40M today
In my base case Emrosi reaches $200M and bull case $400M
That's all we need
So the legacy revenue lasting until Emrosi really picks up is all we need, then it simply won't matter for the thesis.
